It also says political survival of Putin and his coalition became a countrywide task, which fits personality-cult and loyalty-management dynamics.","question_ids":["4B.5","4B.3","4B.4"]},{"title":"Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024","summary":"Looking back at 2023, Freedom House says the Putin regime intensified propaganda to maintain support, used patriotic and militaristic narratives, and kept civic expression constrained. That is militarized spectacle and a loyalty test, not institutional neutrality.","question_ids":["4B.5","3B.9"]},{"title":"Russia’s Duma raises treason to a life sentence","publisher":"Reuters","date":"18 Apr 2023","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russian-parliament-votes-to-introduce-life-sentences-for-treason-3058140","summary":"Reuters reported the Duma raising treason to life imprisonment and increasing penalties for terrorism and sabotage. In context, this looks like coercive legal hardening for political discipline and intimidation rather than neutral legal administration.","question_ids":["4B.5","3B.8"]},{"title":"Russia designates The Moscow Times newspaper a “foreign agent”","publisher":"Reuters","date":"18 Nov 2023","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/russia-designates-the-moscow-times-newspaper-a-foreign-agent-3238256","summary":"The Justice Ministry designated an independent newspaper a foreign agent, adding disclosure burdens and restrictions after it had already been blocked. This is a clear example of politicizing a supposedly neutral state body against independent media.","question_ids":["4B.5","4B.3"]},{"title":"Russia arrests leader of vote monitoring group three weeks before regional polls","publisher":"Reuters","date":"18 Aug 2023","url":"https://theprint.in/world/russia-arrests-leader-of-vote-monitoring-group-three-weeks-before-regional-polls/1720660/","summary":"Reuters said the arrest of Golos co-chair Grigory Melkonyants and raids on monitors’ homes appeared aimed at blocking scrutiny of the vote.
